It's undoubtedly a disappointing result for Alive Inc, whose headcount is " about five " according to the studio. It's also possible the studio was blindsided by the backlash: this Pew Research Center survey places South Korea as the least AI sceptical nation among 25 countries surveyed, including the US, the UK, Australia and India. According to MIT Technology Review , the South Korean government has overwhelmingly embraced AI. It even tried to roll out AI-powered school textbooks (which failed).

Half (or in some cases, slightly less) of those surveyed in the US, Italy, Australia and Brazil are "more concerned than excited" by AI use in daily life. In South Korea, those "more concerned than excited" by AI make up only 16 percent.
There's a trace of surprise in the inevitable statement made by studio director Young Kim, who promised the AI-generated cutscenes would be replaced "by this weekend" (this has already happened).

(Image credit: Alive Inc) "If someone asked me what I think about using AI, the honest answer is that I would have to think about it for a long time," the director wrote. "The reason I chose AI was that I believed it could reach a level of expression our existing resources could not, and that it would let us focus more on the game itself, outside of story and cinematics."

He continued: "That was a hasty judgment on my part. Unless AI takes one more leap and reaches a point where no one can tell the difference, what I believed was still closer to an ideal than a reality. I expected some of you would be disappointed by our use of AI. I did not expect it to become this big."

The statement then hits upon a question that will be raised again and again in the coming months and years concerning creative work: if AI can do it better, why not? In this instance, it unambiguously could not: the cutscenes, and I've seen them, are quintessential slop, and compare very unfavourably to the in-game art. Young Kim says the studio originally composed the cutscenes in-engine, but later replaced them with AI. Somehow, his team didn't detect this chasm.

"The truth is, we spent a long time trying to tell this game's story with cutscenes made entirely by our own hands," the statement goes on. "The results were devastating every time. We came to believe we could not properly deliver this game's complex, difficult narrative that way, and that is why we turned to AI. But if that choice hurt your experience, the fault is not in the tool. It is in our own shortcomings."

Alive Inc joins a long list of studios who have reneged on AI use after extreme public backlash, including Larian Studios and Sandfall Interactive. Vapor World isn't wholesale slop—the studio worked hard on the core game and it shows—but the outcry surrounding its launch does show that using generative AI to cut corners isn't, for now, something audiences are willing to tolerate.

据公共技术线专家曾子骄的现场分享，目前他们已经形成了一套叫做Motus AI的3D角色动画生成大模型矩阵，贯穿角色动画生产全链路，涵盖骨骼生成、蒙皮生成、文本/视频生动作、关键帧插帧、动作精修、实时智能驱动等诸多功能。
具体而言，传统的动画制作流程，是花三周时间，搞定原画→模型→绑定→动画。但有了Motus之后，这边输入原画，那边Agent用一天就能输出模型到蒙皮，再到绑定的结果，直接拿去动捕、验证和设计动画。这样动画可以提前两周开始跑，等三周后传统管线交付正式资产时，在交汇节点直接替换，让开发节奏大概提前两周。

还有一个细节，是如何让不同项目组都愿意改造自己的工具链， 不断给 反馈 ，以此不断强化Motus的能力。因为要提升模型质量，专家反馈必不可少。但如果让一批顶尖游戏人不做项目，专门 做 标注，这个ROI显然不太划算，最好是能把工作中的每一次操作都利用起来。
所以说，单一生产环节、个别项目的优化，只是AI for Game的开始。在陈冬看来，未来1-2年，包括在Motus在内的AI工具要尽可能接触更多的项目， 最终收束成3-4条通用路线，方便更多团队使用它们， 从而 生成更高质量的模型， 并基于更多的数据， 让模型自我迭代。
而且这种兴奋，正在扩散到更大的领域。比如一位动画方向的大学教授在听了Motus的分享后，感慨高校要正视AI已经参与到管线当中的事实。他们需要把变化纳入课程体系，重新思考动画人才该如何培养。我想只有产学研的通路彻底闭环，这最后一公里才算真正完成。
AI in Game
所谓 AI in Game，指的是在游戏中运用AI，提升玩家的体验，甚至创造新的玩法。 这是行业对AI寄予厚望的另一大原因。
说实话，我一直觉得这个领域是中国 游戏 厂商 的 “ 专利 ” ……毕竟GDC上，腾讯、网易等大厂曾多次分享类似领域的突破。从一开始能打好《王者荣耀》的 绝悟 AI，到 《和平精英》 可观察战局、可实时语音交互的AI队友 小田 ，再到 《洛克王国 ：世界 》 的 游戏原生 AI Coach Agent 。坐拥大DAU游戏的我们，似乎天然就擅长这个方向。

不过有意思的是，来自腾讯游戏公共技术线GIGA （General Instructable Game Agent） 团队的杨敬文，这次分享了一个更加超前的方向：他们提出了一个Autonomous Agent Framework （自主智能体架构） ，让智能体不仅可以被玩家指挥，还可以在不同游戏之间迁移，也就是具备更通用的能力。 按照G amescom dev AI议题联合策划人Tommy 的说法， GIGA 探索了其他 游戏团队 尚未涉足的领域， 他很希望大家知道在其他地方正在发生什么事情 。
具体来说，GIGA采用了双脑架构。首先，它会理解游戏的规则，描述自己当前面对的态势，然后根据不同情形的关键指标，在玩法数据库里检索依据，并利用大模型的推理能力决策出意图，再由对应的专家skill小模型 （比如自动驾驶专家） 决定具体的行动。
和传统智能NPC不同，这个模型不只能理解和执行指令，陪伴玩家，还能深刻理解战局，形成有逻辑的决策链路。而且和人类一样，智能体可以迁移诸如利用掩体、跑跳、找点位等基础能力，胜任各种各样的游戏。如果真能实现，很多游戏的底层设计、玩法机制，甚至传播路径 （比如能不能让AI主播玩出花来？） 可能都要变了。
在这方面，杨敬文的观点很有代表性：没有任何事情逼他们做GIGA，但就像没有人任何人逼ChatGPT做大模型：如果一直不做，他们有一天就可能被动，甚至被革命掉。
Game for AI
不少大佬都已达成共识， AI in Game的终极目标，是 在虚拟世界中实现具身智能，并让智能体在长周期中实现自主目的 ，最终涌现出像《头号玩家》那样的虚实结合的世界，以及与之相关的新玩法。
ARC隶属于公共技术线 ，他们最大的任务是看清未来，为之备战，同时提升腾讯的技术影响力。下一代智能体 ， 正好也 是他们最重要的研究方向 之一 。
作为资深科学家，单瀛很认可GIGA的技术方向——想让智能体变得更加通用，可能需要智能体像人类一样，真正用视觉面对原始信息，理解世界、物理规律和空间结构，而不是靠"作弊"理解一切，直接切入底层数据。
据单瀛介绍，这条路线的挑战远比传统智能体更大。传统智能体的"作弊"不是没有理由：结构化数据传输的数据量小，处理负担也小；如果用图像传输，客户端渲染、图像数据传输和图像处理的开销都要解决。而且作为玩家的队友或对手，AI还要渲染不一样的画面。
事情这么难，为什么还要做？这里面多少带着一点责任感甚至是使命感……用一句话说， 陈冬和 单瀛 都认为， 游戏会是AGI（通用人工智能）之路至关重要的 一把 钥匙 。 原因如下：
第二，游戏天然具备「世界-智能体-行动-反馈」的闭环，且状态可观测、规则可控制、过程可重置，因此不受真实世界中安全、成本和硬件条件的限制；
所以，游戏比现实的成本低，又比模拟器更真实，且支持大规模的人类反馈，这天然就是 助力实现 AGI的试验场。用单瀛的话说，“以后哪个团队说自己在做世界模型或者NPC智能体，你先看看它背后有没有游戏业务。”
如今几年过去，大语言模型和生成式AI的发展，让陈冬曾经的梦想变成了现实。但他始终记得那种只能作壁上观的感觉。他的反思是，必须掌握核心技术，从底层解决问题。
从这个角度看，虽然今年的GDC和gamescom dev证明，我们对于AI 的 落地生产 实践，对于智能体的探索正在引领全球行业的发展。但在这个行业， 比起流水争先， 整个产业，甚至跨行业技术创新的滔滔不绝，才是繁荣的前提。
陈冬也认为，一城一地、一朝一夕的领先并不重要。因为 AI所带来的机会远不止于此。AI +引擎，AI+组织…… 太多维度的机会都在等待被人发现。

matched_paragraphs: How many times do some of the most creative and respected figures in this industry need to explain not only why AI is not the key to making a good game, but that it's actually detrimental to creativity? Or as Dispatch's creative director cleanly put: "maybe it's a creative solution if you aren't creative".

We've seen Larian's lead writer trash talk it, saying that AI-generated text is "a 3/10 at best" . PUBG founder Brendan Greene has explained how "it's like a race to the middle of shit" as AI content becomes less and less trustworthy. When asked how Take-Two uses AI to help make successful games its CEO, Zelnick, simply said "clones don't sell" . Hell, even the king of overpromising Peter Molyneux is tepid when it comes to using it .

(Image credit: Devolver Digital) But here we are, beating the same damn horse that just won't die as The Talos Principle 3's writers explain why they're also cautious about AI, the lies it tries to sell, and its actual impact on this industry.

(Image credit: Devolver Digital) Kyratzes notes that it's not a clear-cut situation, though, as the technology itself "has a number of very interesting applications" which are unfortunately overshadowed by "these excessive quasi-religious claims" which are "not rooted in any kind of reality." Such as DeepMind's CEO claiming that humanity will experience widespread change that's "10 times bigger than the Industrial Revolution" or Altman saying the AI singularity is already upon us .

"I think a lot of them are also mainly just meant to juice up the stock market," Kyratzes adds. "It's so complicated because the current AI conversation is kind of a bit strange in that some of the time we're talking about something that we call AI, but it's not artificial general intelligence. It's LLMs or machine learning in various forms, which aren't necessarily the same as artificial intelligence in the sense of conscious being."

Kyratzes is right: We've gotten into the unhealthy habit of referring to everything that sits under the 'AI umbrella' as AI, when in a lot of cases, the actual technology is either vastly different than what we're describing it to be, has already been alive and kicking in the industry for years now, or is simply not as ground-breaking as some would have you believe.

(Image credit: Devolver Digital) "I'm with Jonas in that the LLMs that we're currently dealing with, they're basically incredibly intelligent versions of the autocorrect that I have on my phone," narrative designer Verena Kyratzes says. "And calling them actual AI, general AI, is just ludicrous. I think in the current system that we have, it's just a plagiarism machine that makes people lose their jobs. But I want to have hope that it's a good thing. It's very troublesome to me."

But even still AI isn't a total write-off for Kyratzes, especially since AI isn't even the sole catalyst for some of the most pressing issues which have risen around it. "I'm not against any technology in and of itself," he adds. "So, to me, a lot of the questions are not questions of the technology.

"For example, when a lot of jobs are being lost because of AI, I don't think that that's an AI issue. I think that's a labour issue. That is, why is the power of labour relative to capital so weak? So low that we can't defend ourselves against the owners just eliminating everyone? Like, what's happened to, you know, militant labor, for example. Where is that?"

matched_paragraphs: Services provider Side has signed a memorandum of understanding with Danish AI firm Modl.ai.
The MOU is binding for six months and will see the two companies working together on an AI-enabled quality assurance system.

Side – formerly PTW – is a long-time player in the services space. Meanwhile, Modl.ai is a newer entrant to the games market. Founded in 2018, the company raised $1.7 million in seed funding two years later .

"The MOU effectively brings the best of what Side has and the best of what Modl.ai has together in a unique solution," Side's chief commercial officer Martin McBride says. "One of the crown jewel, holy grail experiences for the games industry right now has been using AI technology to better augment QA services. No one's really found a great solution for that. We think we have."
Saber Interactive CEO responds to claims that a writer was replaced with AI

Previous AI-enabled QA tech – including that created by Modl.ai – involved developers having to send over entire builds for quality assurance companies for the tech to test. Modl.ai's solution used to be "integration-based" with a plugin and SDK and required developers to provide source code. Unsurprisingly, this created too much friction and "became difficult over time", according to the company's founder Christoffer Holmgard.

"We take the product as you would give it to a QA tester, as you would eventually give it to the consumer," he says. "You put it on a very similar or even the same device. And then our solution plays the game by looking at the screen, simulating key processes, generating a data set of everything that happens, and then hands it over to a second AI system that has a look at it and identifies bugs, raises it up to the human level and asks whether this is something we should act on."
The first step in the process is what Modl.ai calls building "game knowledge". Developers can upload assets from their project and talk to the AI to build up their 'understanding' of the game.
After that, developers define what they want to test. This can vary from "classic test cases" to creating new things that are more "suitable for the AI system".
"This is where you need some human expertise here to adapt to the prompting and the language to the AI agent to make it do the right things," Holmgard explains.
From there, the system generates bug reports based on their session – or run, as Modl.ai calls it – with data produced.

One thing that an AI might find tricky to figure out is whether something in a game is a bug or a feature. Holmgard says that feedback from QA testers will, in part, help the AI system understand the nuances of game design.
In fact, Side envisions a future where QA staff move into being AI engineers. In doing so, this will change where quality assurance jobs are done globally.

"One of the cool parts about programs like this is that we get to move our people up the value chain," McBride explains. "So instead of just doing testing and having a career at Side being a tester and moving up to being a senior tester and all the way up, they can become an AI engineer. And so it allows our people to get paid more money. It allows us to have new career paths. And it allows us to potentially bring jobs back to countries and areas where these jobs historically have gone away due to price points and labour concerns. When they're moved back up the value chain, we can move them back into countries where they have historically left."
"This tool really does allow our people to take the best of what AI can offer and reduce the burden and also reduce mistake"
McBride goes on to say that using AI will allow QA testers to have a more "fulfilling career" at Side, as the tech is intended to handle some of the more repetitive and boring work.

Modl.ai's chief product officer Benedikte Mikkelsen adds: "There are some very tedious tests that testers are performing right now. You don't really need a human doing the same flow over and over again. That person could be doing something much more valuable, like assessing the gameplay itself or doing more creative kinds of testing. That, I think, is a value proposition [of using AI]."
McBride also emphasises that AI is not a replacement for QA workers. In fact, he says it will "move people up the value chain".
McBride adds that Side views AI as a "sliding scale", going on to say that "there will always be a human in the loop".

"That's sort of our ethos," he says. "But this tool really does allow our people to take the best of what AI can offer and reduce the burden and also reduce mistakes. I mean, a lot of this work is tedious and a lot of it. People are prone to making mistakes in human error. You take that out of the equation, and everything kind of just ratchets up a notch and it becomes better."

Asked what type of game this AI solution works with, Side's chief operating officer Oliver Deslandes is candid that the tech right now works with more simplistic titles; that is, not 3D open-world adventures, but rather smaller experiences.

The really brain-melting thing though is that Kress adds that the company expects "to grow revenue by approximately 70% in fiscal 2028," even in the midst of the RAMpocalypse . matched_paragraphs: Linux creator Linus Torvalds has famously been fairly hot and cold on generative AI in coding work, seeing a good purpose for it whilst also acknowledging a lack of quality control has led to a flood of unhelpful reports . Well, it seems like AI won't be fully replacing him just yet, as he's recently undergone a 'debug session from hell' where his AI assistant recommended he give up several times.

This is a good example of where an AI might struggle to fix code, because it's not a syntax error or a bug, necessarily. The function is technically 'correct', it's just not doing what Torvalds wants it to . "The AI several times stated flat out that this was impossible and unsolvable," says Torvalds, "and that we should just write a report about it."

It seems like grit, determination, and stubbornness were what got the AI to behave in the end. Torvalds says, "I suspect those things have been trained by people who may not be quite as stubborn as I am."

Torvalds does praise the AI he's using, noting that, "while the AI was ready to give up several times, it did keep adding debug code and analyzing it faithfully when I pushed. So credit where credit is due and I let the AI write the commit message above."

Linus Torvalds says tracking down a bug in Linux's Intel GFX Driver was a "debug session from hell." Generative AI in coding has proved to be somewhat contentious. Last year, Collins Dictionary awarded 'vibe coding' (coding with AI) the word of the year , and a paper at the beginning of 2026 argued that " vibe coding kills open source " due to the lack of human attention and the ability for anyone to contribute huge amounts of data.

AI vibe coding ports of old console games have even become a bit of an ethical battleground . The team behind DK64 Randomizer (as you might guess, it randomises Donkey Kong 64) has been developing an unofficial PC port, specifically saying "Fuck AI vibe coding bullshit."

That's because, ignoring environmental concerns of AI plus the ethically dubious sourcing of data for training , teams like DK64 Randomizer argue that reliance on vibe coding results "in a poor quality project that will make it progressively harder to manage as time goes on."
Some developers clearly argue the benefit of AI code right now, but even so, it seems a human touch is often needed.

这件事值得大家重点关注的地方在于：成熟的效率工具类 App 不再只等待用户主动打开 App 界面，而是开始把自身核心业务能力开放给 AI Agent 调用。开发者需要重新设计动作接口、授权流程以及商店产品页面描述的逻辑。
AI Agent 是能够自主规划、调用工具并执行动作，以及自主完成复杂任务的智能系统。普通 AI 聊天只能给出回答，但 Agent 还可以直接执行操作，例如搜索文件、保存资料、生成分享链接等。
根据夸克网盘的 App Store 版本说明，用户可以在 App 内复制 Skill 安装指令，发送给 AI Agent，再完成安装和账号授权。官方信息显示，该能力支持阿里千问、腾讯WorkBuddy等 AI Agent 产品。 官方开放的操作能力包含文件存储、下载、备份、分享、转存、移动，还有智能搜索、相册整理、知识问答等功能。
七麦数据监测显示，截至 8 月 27 日 10 时，夸克网盘位列中国大陆 App Store 效率免费榜第 7 名。榜单前十当中，既有豆包、千问、DeepSeek这类 AI 智能助手产品，也有百度网盘、QQ 邮箱、迅雷这类效率工具。
从这份榜单可以看到，AI 助手和效率工具正在争夺同一批用户。
当下有一种观点，认为 AI Agent 会替代一部分工具类 App。但夸克网盘释放出的信号给出另一种可能性：工具 App 的界面打开频次或许会下降，但账户、文件数据、会员权益、业务操作能力依旧保留在 App 服务内部。
第三，增长团队要注意重新设计商店产品页面的文案。 不要简单写 “支持 AI”。更有效的写法是讲清楚 AI 可以帮用户完成什么任务、需要获取哪些权限、处理完成后的结果保存在哪里。新能力上线阶段，可以借助 App Store 应用内活动展示真实使用场景，同时利用自定产品页面，针对不同用户群体输出差异化的页面内容。
结合国内 App Store 效率类 App 榜单、夸克网盘版本说明以及官方公开资料来看 ，AI 工具的竞争重心，正在从 “谁拥有聊天对话入口” 转向 “谁能够承接完成用户任务”。 传统效率工具 App 并不会被简单替代，它们手握账号、数据、权限与成熟服务能力，反而非常适合充当 AI Agent 的执行层。
效率工具 App 的新流量入口，不一定在 App 首页，也有可能出现在另一款 AI 的对话框之中。
